28                                      AURORA

<meta>continues from previous page: ...cury</meta> <note>The text continues the discussion of failed attempts to fix mercury.</note> for itself. Indeed, arsenic certainly cannot be fixed at all unless the artist operator has an equal knowledge of its coloring spirit, regarding which all philosophers have slumbered, attempting in vain to accomplish something from it. Therefore, whoever is ignorant of this spirit should have no hope of fixing it, nor of attributing to it the virtue by which it might acquire the perfection of transmutation. For this reason, I make it known to all that the whitening about which mention has been made is taken from a false foundation, and by it, copper is falsely whitened, not transmuted. The <term>sophistae</term> <gloss>sophists/pseudo-alchemists</gloss>, having thus masked and painted Venus <note>In alchemy, Venus represents copper.</note>, mixed it with a double amount of lunar <note>In alchemy, lunar refers to silver.</note> material, and sold it to goldsmiths and moneyers. Ultimately, however, they transformed themselves into false moneyers, not only those who sold it but also those who bought it. Some of the sophists, in place of white, took red arsenic, and this also went into a false art. For in whatever way it may be prepared, it exhibits nothing except whiteness. Some have proceeded further, to common sulfur, which they cooked in such a yellow state with vinegar, lye, or very sharp urines, day and night, until it emerged white. Afterward, they elevated it from common salt and egg-shell lime through sublimation, and cooked and sublimated it, and did so many times; nevertheless, it remained always combustible, although white. <summary>The author warns against fraudulent alchemical practices, specifically the use of arsenic and sulfur to create a superficial, "sophistic" whiteness in metals, which lacks the stability required for true transmutation.</summary>
